_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. governance.md is preserved by onboard.py --resume but a FULL reprint re-runs gen_governance.py and would re-introduce the mis-tiering.

handfixes.summary: Pipedrive uses `add` as its create verb; the Write tier hand-includes every `<resource> add` create (gen_governance's WRITE keywords omit `add`)
handfixes.why: gen_governance.py's WRITE keyword tuple is (create,update,patch,comment,ignore,archive,reactivate,triage,clear,set) - it does NOT include `add`. Pipedrive uses `add` as the create verb (`deals add`, `persons add`, `organizations add`, `notes add`, `activities add`, `leads add`, `products add`, ...), so EVERY create fell into NO tier -> silently Read (false-negative). The governance Write tier was hand-corrected from the authoritative pp:method to include all 73 routine writes (the `add` creates + `update` + verb-less `import`). A full reprint re-runs gen_governance and drops every `add` create back to Read. See project_gen_governance_missing_add_verb.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Make gen_governance method-aware off agent-context pp:method (would fix add/verb-less/setup at once). Until then every add-verb (Pipedrive-shaped) API needs this hand-correction.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For pipedrive the manifest gained: PIPEDRIVE_BASE_URL. server.json gained: PIPEDRIVE_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: PIPEDRIVE_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer refuses filesystem-destination flags (--db, --input, --output, --out, --home, --audit-dir, --receipt-file and friends) and any argument name carrying '=', so a tool call cannot point the local SQLite store, or any other file this account can reach, at a path of its choosing
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the server account and forwarded every command-local flag straight through as a CLI argument. `sync` and the other local-store commands expose --db, and the store's migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS resources_fts` plus a resources-table rebuild against whatever file it is handed, so one tool call shaped {"db": "/path/to/someone-elses.sqlite"} rewrote an unrelated database - no credentials required, because sync opens the store before it ever reaches the API. Proven end to end: against the pre-fix binary a single MCP tools/call on `sync` changed the victim file's sha and left resources_fts with 0 rows; against the patched binary the same call returns the same sync summary and the victim file is byte-identical. The gate has three parts, all in cli/internal/mcp/cobratree/shellout.go: blockedDestinationFlags (the runtime name floor, unioned into cliArgsFromMCP alongside the pre-existing blockedRootFlags behaviour, which is unchanged); an argument-name '=' guard, because "db=/tmp/evil" was emitted as --db=/tmp/evil and a name-only denylist never saw it; and isFilesystemPathFlag, which classifies a flag by its USAGE TEXT rather than its NAME. The usage-text test is load bearing and must not be turned into a name rule: the generated command surface carries API body fields called --path, --seed-path, --source-paths, --exclude-paths, --filename and --working-dir whose values go to the vendor API and never touch this account's disk, so a name rule would break real API surfaces while still missing the next generated flag that does take a local path. UnblockedFilesystemPathFlags applies that rule to the live Cobra tree over exactly the command set RegisterAll turns into shell-out tools (endpoint and framework commands are out of scope, which is what keeps the rule off generated vendor body fields), and TestNoShellOutToolCanDirectAFilesystemPath fails the build when a regeneration grows a local-path flag the floor does not name. vendorAPIPathFlags is the documented exception list for flags whose usage trips the rule but which name a location in the vendor's world. Both directions are pinned by the tests: the --db argument must be dropped AND an ordinary flag must still be forwarded, because a gate that swallows the real MCP surface is as harmful as one that misses the defect.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the gate belongs in the generator. Two known residuals a reprint should close rather than re-inherit. (1) On the pre-4.30 cobratree the blocked flags are dropped at forward time but still appear in the tool's input schema, because toolOptionsForFlags in typemap.go advertises every flag; the caller gets silence instead of an error. The 4.30 shape (blockedStructuredArgsForCommand + allowedStructuredArgsForCommand) removes them from the schema and errors on them, which is the better behaviour. (2) isFilesystemPathFlag is only consulted by the package test here, not at request time, because the pre-4.30 shellOutToCLI receives no *cobra.Command; wiring it into the per-command blocked set (as skills/servosity does) makes a newly generated path flag refused at runtime rather than at CI time.

handfixes.summary: Both who-command activity fixtures that must sit in the future (the open next-activity, and the future-dated done activity in the ORDER BY regression) are computed as now + 1 year rather than the literals 2030-01-01 and 2099-01-01
handfixes.why: This is the same class of TEST defect that PR #300 fixed in quickbooks, found by that PR's fleet-wide sweep of every YYYY-MM-DD literal under skills/*/cli/internal/**/*_test.go and reported-but-not-fixed there. The command under test reads the wall clock; the fixture pinned an absolute date. That pairing is only true until the calendar reaches the literal, at which point the assertion inverts and the test fails on the date rather than on a code change. queryWho formats time.Now().UTC() as '2006-01-02 15:04:05' and uses it twice: the last-activity query takes the newest done activity due at or before now (or any activity already past due), and the next-activity query takes the earliest not-done activity due now or later. Two fixtures depended on their literal still being in the future. (1) TestNovelWho_LastActivityIgnoresFutureDatedDone seeded a 'Future done' activity at 2099-01-01 to prove it must not outrank a recent past one; in 2099 that row becomes the NEWEST PAST done activity, wins the DESC ordering, and the regression test asserts the exact opposite of its own name. (2) TestNovelWho_QueryWho seeded its open follow-up at 2030-01-01 and asserts next_activity is that row; in 2030 the row stops satisfying due_date >= now, next_activity goes nil, and the assertion fires. Both are now derived from the clock - now-24h for the past done row, now+1y for the two future rows - so the relationship the tests are about is preserved by construction rather than by the calendar. The second site was not in PR #300's report; it was found while working the first and is the same defect in the same file, so it is fixed here rather than left to rot for four more years. String comparison equals chronological comparison because both sides are zero-padded and the date-only literal sorts correctly against the date-and-time now (a full year of margin dwarfs the shorter-string-is-lesser edge at same-day equality). Proven both directions against the real queryWho: seeding both done rows in the past (the post-2099 equivalent) returns last_activity=a2 and the assertion FAILS; the clock-derived seeding returns last_activity=a1 and PASSES.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the acceptance/novel test templates should never emit an absolute date literal whose truth depends on the calendar not having reached it. A fixture that means 'in the future' or 'recently' must be rendered as an offset from a single clock read, the way this fix does it. Same retro as the quickbooks novel-acceptance-fixtures-relative-to-today entry. File via /printing-press-retro.
